description: E2b's Filter rack prefab, built from the same primitives its generator uses (SE16/scripts/build-prefabs.py). Keep this case's script in step with the 'TIDE Filter' entry in PREFABS there. UNLIKE the other prefab cases this one needs a SOURCE as well as the module under test: a filter fed DC measures nothing, so the Oscillator prefab's own recipe drives it. That makes this a two-module case in the same way voice_midi_note is a whole-chain case -- an oscillator regression fails it too, which is a deliberate trade for measuring the filter on a real signal. WHAT IT LOCKS is the filter's defining number: the cutoff jack sits at 5 V, which on the 1 V/octave scale the oscillator shares is 440 Hz, i.e. EXACTLY the source frequency, so the render is the textbook -3 dB AT CUTOFF point of a 1-pole filter. That single number moves if the coefficient math, the sample-rate scaling or the 1 V/octave mapping regresses. Measured 2026-08-19 (macos) across the whole control range on a 440 Hz source, which is why 5 V was chosen as the most informative point rather than an arbitrary one: cutoff 10 V (14 kHz) peak -6.3 dBFS, effectively open; 8 V (3.5 kHz) -6.6 dBFS; 5 V (440 Hz) -9.5 dBFS, the -3 dB point; 2 V (55 Hz) -22.2 dBFS, ~6 dB/octave beyond cutoff. NOTE THE PREFAB ITSELF DEFAULTS THIS JACK TO 10, NOT 5 -- an unpatched rack module must pass signal, the same rule the Envelope's GATE default follows -- so this case deliberately drives the jack to a value the shipped prefab does not default to. It is testing the filter, not the default. POSITIVE CONTROL, measured: change the cutoff --set-pin from 5 to 2 and the case FAILS the null test loudly, so it is sensitive to what the filter actually does rather than merely to audio being present. The relaxed gates below are prefab_oscillator's, verbatim and for its reason, because the same free-running oscillator is in this signal path.
tolerance_reason: Measured on Linux x86_64 (Ubuntu 24.04, glibc 2.39) against this case's reference, SynthEditCL V1.6.192, 2026-08-23 (E1c): null -121.4 dBFS, peakdiff -90.3 dBFS = 1 LSB. Same story and same positive control as prefab_oscillator (old gates blind to a localized glitch up to 26 LSB; defaults catch it from 2), and the same refuted justification -- the core Oscillator at 5 V is rounding class. Now at the defaults. ONE CAVEAT THIS CASE CARRIES AND prefab_oscillator DOES NOT: its reference provenance is recorded 'unknown', so the platform pair is not documented. It is INFERRED cross-platform rather than known: the three references known to be Linux-seeded all rendered bit-identical (-inf) in this same run, so a -121.4 dBFS residual means this reference was almost certainly seeded somewhere else. Strong evidence, not proof -- an older engine on Linux is not excluded, though V1.6.192 reproduced V1.6.186's Linux renders exactly. NOT VERIFIED: the reverse direction, as above.
